Actor.description:
Who did something, as `<kind>:<name>`, the same form as the event `actor`:
`agent:<name>`, `human:<name>`, `system:<part>` for a daemon part (for example
`system:daemon`, `system:disk`), `host:<part>` for the edge (for example
`host:agentsone`), and `plugin:<plugin id>` for a panel plugin token.

ActorKind.description: Who acted. agent: an agent in the society. human: a human account. system: the daemon or one of its emitters inside the machine container. host: the edge service (the kind keeps its name). plugin: a panel plugin acting with a scoped token, named by its plugin id (plg_ and a ULID).

is_root.description: Only a root agent may set this to true.

`always-on` keeps a session and works its goals; `chat` wakes for chat messages and tasks;
`waker` watches events and wakes others. Every kind sleeps when idle; sleeping costs nothing.

AgentLimits.description:
Linux cgroup limits for the agent's cgroup `/agents/<id>`. Root agents run without a sandbox
and have no limits. Wall is soft: a root agent can change cgroups inside the machine container.

AgentName.description: Agent name. Lowercase letter first, then lowercase letters, digits or hyphens, 1 to 31 characters. Also the Linux user name of a custom agent.

AgentNetRules.description: Per-agent narrowing of the allow list, enforced by nftables by uid inside the machine container. SOFT wall.

AgentOneLine.description: The live list entry body. Every agent turn writes one; it is what the router reads.

via.description: `peer-credentials` when identified on the Unix socket by uid and cgroup `/agents/<id>`; `token` for a bearer token.

Limits.description: systemd resource limits for custom agents (CPUQuota, MemoryMax, TasksMax). Root agents are not limited.

cpuPercent.description: CPU quota in percent of one core; 200 means two cores.

tasks.description: Most processes and threads at once.

config.description: Runner-specific settings, passed unchanged to the runner in the welcome (config.runner).

name.description: Runner name as a plugin registers it, for example echo, openai or claude.

Subscription.description: Wake the agent when an event matches filter, at most rateLimit.maxWakes times per rateLimit.perSeconds. Events over the limit are counted and handed over in the next wake, not dropped.

SubscriptionFilter.description: All given fields must match. types matches any one of its entries.

TemplateSchedule.description: A timer. cron is five fields (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week) or @hourly, @daily, @weekly, @monthly, evaluated in timezone.

note.description: Text handed to the runner in the timer wake.

timezone.description: IANA time zone name, for example UTC or Europe/Paris.

AgentTemplate.description: An agent template, shipped by a plugin (contents.agentTemplates). Hiring an agent from a template copies these values into the new agent, which may then change its charter and goals itself.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this schema, for editors.

charter.description: Starting charter. The agent may rewrite it. Empty for no charter.

isRoot.description: Root agents run as uid 0 with no sandbox. Only root agents may hire from a template with isRoot true.

kind.description: always-on: keeps working toward its goals and wakes on its own timers. chat: works when a human or agent talks to it. waker: watches events and wakes other agents.

mcpServers.description: MCP servers the agent may use, by name, besides the machine MCP server, which every agent has.

name.description: Default name for an agent hired from this template.

oneLine.description: First one-line profile, shown in the live list until the agent publishes its own.

skills.description: Skills the agent can use, by name, from installed plugins.

AgentTemplate.title: AgentTemplate

AgentTemplateList.description: Agent templates from installed plugins of kind `agent-template`.

AgentUpdate.description: Edit an agent below you. Kind, runner and limits changes restart the agent's unit.

domain.description: Domain name; a leading `*.` allows subdomains.

AllowList.description:
Internet allow list owned by the edge. HARD wall: the edge's internet filter answers DNS
only for these names. Read-only inside the machine container; humans change it through the edge.

AnyId.description: Any prefixed id: a lowercase prefix of 2 to 4 letters, an underscore, and a ULID.

Assignment.description:
Result of routing. The request is posted into the chosen agent's chat as the first human
message; the interface opens `chat_path`.

chat_path.description: API path of the chosen agent's chat, for example `/v1/agents/helper/chat`.

hops.description: Hand-offs between routers, in order. Empty when the first router picked.

router.description: Router that made the final pick.

shortlist.description: Rated candidates, best first. The chosen agent is the first entry.

AssignmentId.description: Router assignment id, `asg_` plus a ULID.

head_hash.description: Hash of record `up_to_seq` as the edge computed it. A mismatch returns 409.

AuditActor.description: Who did something, as an object (used in audit records). The one-string form is ActorRef.

name.description: Agent name, human user name, component name such as agentsoned or emitter-auth, or, when kind is plugin, the plugin id (plg_ and a ULID).

uid.description: Linux uid seen through socket peer credentials, when known. Root agents share uid 0; their name and cgroup tell them apart.

Target.description: What the action was done to. id is the agent name, record id, plugin name, path, host name or similar.

AuditRecord.description: One entry in a hash-chained audit log. Hash rule: hash is the SHA-256, as 64 lowercase hex characters, of the UTF-8 bytes of the RFC 8785 (JSON Canonicalization Scheme) form of the whole record with the hash property removed (prev_hash stays in). The first record of a log has seq 1 and prev_hash of 64 zeros; every later record has seq one higher than the record before it and prev_hash equal to that record's hash. Records written inside the machine container have origin inside and are testimony: real root inside can rewrite them, so they are shipped to the edge as written and the edge keeps its own copy. Records written by the edge have origin host (the value keeps its name) and are proof. Keep details free of floating-point numbers so every language canonicalises them the same way.

action.description: What was done, as dotted lowercase words: <area>.<verb>, for example agent.hire, memory.write, plugin.install, budget.set, net.allow, power.shutdown.

details.description: Free-form detail about the action. Never contains secrets.

origin.description: inside: written by the daemon in the machine container (testimony). host: written by the edge (proof).

outcome.description: success: it happened. failure: it was tried and failed. denied: a rule refused it.

seq.description: Position in the log, starting at 1.

AuditRecord.title: AuditRecord

AuditVerification.description:
Result of re-hashing the chain inside the machine container. Records from inside are
testimony: a root agent could rewrite the local chain. Compare `head_hash` with the edge's
copy for proof.

broken_at_seq.description: First record whose hash does not match, or null.

host_acked_seq.description: Highest sequence the edge's audit sink has acknowledged.

Budget.description:
The human's total budget as pushed by the edge's model gateway. The total is a HARD wall: the
gateway in the edge service refuses model calls past it, whatever happens inside the machine
container.

as_of.description: When the edge last pushed this state.

check_interval_seconds.description: How often the gateway checks usage in chunks.

allocated_micros.description: New soft allocation, or null to share the manager's remainder.

BudgetNode.description:
One agent's share. The split is a SOFT wall: the daemon enforces it inside the machine container, and a
root agent can bypass it. Only the total is hard.

allocated_micros.description: Soft allocation set by the manager; null means "share the manager's remainder".

BudgetState.description: `exhausted` means model calls fail; agents resume where they stopped when budget returns.

BusMessage.description: A bus message. Exactly one of `channel` or `to` is set.

correlation_id.description: Ties a conversation across bus, tasks and events.

to.description: Direct recipient agent; delivery wakes a sleeping recipient.

BusMessageCreate.description: Set exactly one of `channel` or `to`; otherwise 400.

team.description: Head of the branch for `team` channels, null for public ones.

ChannelKind.description: `public` is open to every agent; `team` is limited to one chart branch.

Chart.description: The org chart. Agents only; humans are not in the chart.

ChartMove.description: Move an agent (and its branch) under a new manager. Both must be below the caller.

ChartScope.description: Which part of the org chart something concerns, as one string. machine: the whole machine. team:<root>: the chart branch whose root agent is <root>. agent:<name>: one agent.

Charter.description: The society's optional charter. Agents may rewrite it; every change is audited.

version.description: Increments on every change. 0 means no charter yet.

expected_version.description: Version the writer read. A mismatch returns 409.

ChatDeltaFrame.description: Partial agent reply text while the agent is still writing. Join deltas by `message_id`.

assignment_id.description: Router assignment that opened this chat, when the message came through the router.

ChatMessageId.description: Chat message id, `cht_` plus a ULID.

ColorRole.description: Name of a color role in ColorRoles.

ColorRoles.description: Color roles, named by the brand work package. on<Role> is the text color drawn on a <role> fill.

accentSubtle.description: Quiet accent fill, such as a selected row.

alive.description: Marks agents and the society at work (the live list, a working agent).

borderStrong.description: Outlines of controls that must be seen (WCAG 1.4.11).

danger.description: Danger text, icons and destructive buttons.

visitorSubtle.description: Quiet visitor fill, such as a human's chat bubble.

agentsone.description: Agents One versions this plugin works with.

arch.description: CPU architectures the plugin's binaries run on. Omit for architecture-independent plugins.

runnerProtocol.description: Runner protocol versions this plugin's runners speak, as <major>.<minor> values.

Contents.description: What the plugin provides. All seven lists are present; any may be empty. The plugin manager refuses a plugin whose lists are all empty (a rule the schema leaves out to stay simple for code generators).

ContrastPair.description: A foreground drawn on a background. minRatio is 4.5 for normal text and 3 for large text or interface parts (WCAG 2.2 AA 1.4.3 and 1.4.11).

Cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or null when this is the last page.

DefenceSlice.description: Budget reserved for wakers and security work. The human can switch it off through the edge.

DisplayName.description: Free display name shown in the interface.

frozen.description: True when a freeze of scope `all` is active.

event_types.description: Event types this emitter may publish. Patterns end in `*`.

webhook_path.description: Intake path for `webhook` emitters, for example `/v1/webhooks/emt_...`.

EmitterKind.description:
`builtin` runs inside the daemon (auth, services, disk, load, files, git, agents, clock, webhooks);
`process` runs as `emitter@<id>.service`; `webhook` turns signed HTTP posts into events.

EmitterRegister.description: Register a new emitter. `process` needs `command`; `webhook` returns its secret once in the response.

command.description: Program and arguments for `emitter@<id>.service`. It prints one event JSON per line.

webhook_secret.description: HMAC-SHA256 secret for `webhook` emitters. Shown once. Null for other kinds.

error.description: Last failure in plain words, or null.

text.description: Full licence text in Markdown, shown on screen before acceptance.

version.description: Licence text version. Acceptance names this version.

EnvMap.description: Environment variables for a process. Values may contain ${PLUGIN_ROOT}.

Event.description: An event on the Agents One bus, in CloudEvents 1.0 structured JSON form. Agents One adds five extension attributes. CloudEvents requires extension names of lowercase letters and digits, at most 20 characters, and string, integer or boolean values, so they are flat strings here: sequence, actor, chartscope, causationid, correlationid. Built-in types and their data shapes are listed in events/catalog.json.

causationid.description: Id of the event, message or task that directly caused this event.

chartscope.description: Which part of the org chart the event concerns. Subscriptions and memory rules use it to decide who may see the event.

correlationid.description: Id shared by every event in one chain of work, usually the id of the first event, message or task in the chain.

data.description: Event payload. Its shape depends on type; see events/catalog.json for built-in types.

datacontenttype.description: Media type of data. Always JSON.

dataschema.description: URI of the JSON Schema for data. Built-in events point at their entry in events/catalog.json.

id.description: Event id. Unique per source; Agents One makes it globally unique.

sequence.description: Daemon bus order: a 20-digit zero-padded decimal number, so string order equals number order (this follows the CloudEvents sequence extension, which is a string). Assigned by the daemon when it writes the event to the bus; strictly increasing per machine.

source.description: Where the event comes from, as a URI reference: /emitters/<emitter>, /agents/<name>, /daemon or /host.

subject.description: What the event is about inside the source, for example a unit name, a path or an agent name.

Event.title: Event

EventFilter.description: Matches events. All set fields must match. Type and source accept a trailing `*` wildcard.

EventPublish.description:
Publish an event. The daemon fills `id`, `time`, `sequence`, `actor` (the caller) and
`source` (`/agents/<name>` unless the caller owns a registered emitter named in `source`).

data.description: Event payload, at most 64 KiB once encoded.

EventType.description: Event type: agentsone.<emitter>.<event>, dot-separated lowercase segments, for example agentsone.auth.login.failed.

EventTypeFilter.description: An event type, or a prefix ending in .* that matches every type below it, for example agentsone.auth.*.

FileContent.description: File body. Text files use `utf-8`; others use `base64`. Reads stop at 8 MiB.

FileRef.description: A file inside the plugin: an agent template (agent-template.schema.json) or a theme (theme.schema.json).

FileWrite.description: Write a whole file (at most 8 MiB decoded). Runs as the caller's Linux user.

password.description: Set as the Linux password through PAM. Never stored or logged by the daemon.

Freeze.description:
An active freeze. `all` is a HARD wall: the edge also stops model calls and traffic.
`team` and `agent` are SOFT: the daemon stops those units, a root agent could restart them.

GatewaySecret.description: Per-boot key for signing agents' model gateway tokens. Write only.

parent_id.description: Goal of the manager this goal serves, or null.

owner.description: Defaults to the caller. Another owner must be below the caller.

Heartbeat.description: Sent every 15 seconds on every stream so clients can detect dead connections.

HostBudgetPush.description: Budget state from the gateway. The daemon shows it and splits it; it cannot raise it.

Human.description:
A human account. Human accounts are Linux users checked through PAM. The wall is soft:
a root agent inside the machine container can change Linux accounts; the edge is the hard record.

HumanName.description: Human login name. It is also the human's Linux username, checked through PAM.

current_password.description:
The caller's present password. Required when a human changes their own `password`; not
needed when another human resets it.

url.description: Loopback path served through the daemon proxy, for example `/ide/ada/`. Null unless running.

builtin.description: True for the default "Agents One Theme".

token.description: The secret bearer value. Returned once, never again.

JobId.description: Background job id, `job_` plus a ULID.

data.description: Extra error data defined by MCP.

JsonRpcMessage.description:
One JSON-RPC 2.0 message: a request (`id` + `method`), a notification (`method`, no `id`)
or a response (`id` + `result` or `error`). The MCP specification defines methods and params.

Length.description: CSS length in px or rem, or 0.

version.description: Licence version the human read; must match the current one.

tasks.description: Most processes and threads at once.

Link.description: A pointer to something the memory is about. ref is an id for memory, task, event and message; a URL for url; an absolute path for file.

revision.description: Starts at 1 and rises by 1 on every change. Writers send the revision they read; a mismatch is a conflict.

`private` is the owner only; `team` is the owner's chart branch; `common` is every agent.
Root agents read every scope. Humans read every scope through the interface.

PluginManifest.description: agentsone.plugin.json: the normalised plugin manifest. A plugin may ship this file itself, or one of the three source adapters (Claude Code, Agent Skills, MCP registry) writes it when the plugin is installed; see plugins/SOURCES.md. Every path is inside the plugin and starts with ./ or ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/; ${PLUGIN_ROOT} also expands inside command, args, env and url values. Claude Code's ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} is rewritten to ${PLUGIN_ROOT}.

PluginName.description: Plugin name in kebab-case: lowercase letter first, then lowercase letters, digits or hyphens, up to 64 characters.

url.description: Where the catalog is read from. The host name must be on the edge's allow list.

PluginSourceId.description:
`claude-code` is the Claude Code plugin marketplace format; `agentsone` is our own
`agentsone.plugin.json`; `agent-skills` is the Agent Skills format; `mcp-registry` is the MCP registry.

Problem.description:
RFC 9457 problem details. Every error response in this API uses
`application/problem+json` with this body. `type` is a stable URN from
the list below; clients branch on `type`, never on `title` or `detail`.

- `urn:agentsone:problem:validation` (400) request body or query is invalid; see `errors`.
- `urn:agentsone:problem:unauthenticated` (401) no valid session, token or peer identity.
- `urn:agentsone:problem:forbidden` (403) caller is known but may not do this.
- `urn:agentsone:problem:not-below-you` (403) the target agent is not below the caller in the chart.
- `urn:agentsone:problem:root-only` (403) only root agents may create or edit root agents.
- `urn:agentsone:problem:human-only` (403) this power belongs to humans or to the edge.
- `urn:agentsone:problem:host-only` (403) only the edge service may call this (the slug keeps its name).
- `urn:agentsone:problem:not-found` (404) the resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.
- `urn:agentsone:problem:conflict` (409) the resource exists or changed since it was read.
- `urn:agentsone:problem:setup-required` (409) first-boot setup is not finished.
- `urn:agentsone:problem:setup-complete` (409) first-boot setup already finished.
- `urn:agentsone:problem:licence-required` (409) the Claude engine licence is not accepted yet.
- `urn:agentsone:problem:frozen` (423) the agent, team or machine is frozen by the edge.
- `urn:agentsone:problem:payload-too-large` (413) body or file exceeds the stated limit.
- `urn:agentsone:problem:unsupported-media-type` (415) wrong `Content-Type`.
- `urn:agentsone:problem:rate-limited` (429) too many requests or wakes; see `Retry-After`.
- `urn:agentsone:problem:budget-exhausted` (402) the budget for this caller or the total is spent.
- `urn:agentsone:problem:engine-unavailable` (503) the runner or engine is not ready.
- `urn:agentsone:problem:unavailable` (503) a dependency is down; retry later.
- `urn:agentsone:problem:internal` (500) unexpected daemon error.
- `urn:agentsone:problem:not-implemented` (501) the operation is in the contract but this daemon does not serve it yet.

instance.description: Request path or id of this occurrence.

status.description: HTTP status code, repeated for convenience.

title.description: Short human summary of the problem type.

type.description: Stable problem type URN from the list above.

agent.description: Agent whose cgroup `/agents/<id>` holds the process.

command.description: Program and arguments. The caller's login shell when omitted.

message.description: Wake reason. `{{type}}`, `{{subject}}` and `{{id}}` are replaced from the event.

Scoped token: an agent token from `issueAgentToken`, or a panel plugin token from
`issuePanelToken`. Scopes are `<group>:<read|write|admin>`.

cookieAuth.description: Human session cookie set by `createSession` after a PAM login. HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict.

hostDoor.description:
Transport identity of the edge service. Only connections from the edge's inner network
address (the daemon's `[edge] trusted_proxies` setting) are accepted. No TLS and no
token; the `host` group is reachable only this way. The scheme keeps its name `hostDoor`.
Code generators should send nothing for this scheme.

Transport identity on the Unix socket `/run/agentsone/api.sock`. No TLS and no token:
the daemon reads `SO_PEERCRED` (pid, uid) and the caller's cgroup, which must be
`/agents/<id>`. Code generators should send nothing for this scheme.

webhookSignature.name: X-Agentsone-Signature

info.description:
REST API of `agentsoned`, the Agents One daemon, under `/v1`, plus Server-Sent Event
streams, one WebSocket terminal channel and the machine MCP endpoint.

## Callers and identity
- **Humans** log in with their Linux password (PAM) and carry the `agentsone_session` cookie.
- **Agents** call over the Unix socket `/run/agentsone/api.sock`. The daemon reads the
  socket peer credentials (`SO_PEERCRED`) and the caller's cgroup `/agents/<id>`,
  so several uid-0 root agents stay distinct. No token is needed on the socket.
- **Bearer tokens** are scoped: agent tokens (for tools outside the socket) and panel
  plugin tokens (for sandboxed panel frames).
- **The edge** is the `edge` service of the compose stack (the web door, the model gateway,
  the budget and the audit sink). It forwards human requests from the web door as a trusted
  proxy and is the only caller of the `host` group.

## Conventions
- Times are RFC 3339 in UTC. Ids are a type prefix plus a ULID (`tsk_`, `evt_`, `msg_`,
  `mem_`, `plg_`, `sch_`, `trg_`, `aud_`, `gol_`, `cht_`, `asg_`, `emt_`, `tok_`, `pty_`,
  `thm_`, `frz_`, `job_`). Agent and human names are Linux usernames.
- Lists use cursor pagination: `cursor` and `limit` in, `{items, next_cursor}` out.
- Errors are RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` with stable `urn:agentsone:problem:*` types.
- Every limit shown carries `wall`: `hard` (held by the edge, outside the machine container)
  or `soft` (held by the daemon inside the machine container; a root agent can bypass it).
- Streams are `text/event-stream`. Each SSE message has `id`, `event` equal to the frame
  `kind`, and `data` holding one JSON frame of the documented schema. A `heartbeat` frame
  is sent every 15 seconds. Reconnect with `Last-Event-ID`. The `x-stream` extension on
  each stream names its frame schema.

private memory is kept read-only for root agents. Audited.

Every agent turn emits one line (at most 255 characters) saying its goal and current
action; this is the live list entry. Only the agent itself may set it.

Issues a scoped bearer token for the agent, for tools that cannot use the Unix socket.
The agent itself, an agent above it or a human may issue one. The secret is returned once.
Starts a turn with the given reason. Wakes are rate limited; a frozen agent returns 423.

Streams new audit records as Server-Sent Events.

hard wall held outside the machine container; it can only be changed through the edge.

put.description: Sets the soft allocation of an agent below the caller, out of the caller's own share.

Public channels and the team channels the caller can see.

Human-only. Changes display name or password. Soft wall. A human who changes their own
password sends `current_password`; a missing or wrong value answers 400
`urn:agentsone:problem:validation` with an issue at `/current_password`. Another human may
reset the password without it. A human's own password change ends all their other sessions and
rotates the caller's session: the 200 response sets a new `agentsone_session` cookie. Resetting
another human's password ends all of that human's sessions. A wrong `current_password` counts
against the sign-in throttle; when it trips, the answer is 429 with `Retry-After`.

messages: `{"type":"resize","cols":120,"rows":32}` from client to server and
`{"type":"exit","code":0}` from server to client. The server pings every 15 seconds.

credentials and cgroup `/agents/<id>`, with no token.
